entries.title: Destiny of an Emperor

entries.title: Dick Tracy

entries.title: Die Hard
entries.summary: Activision's top-down NES adaptation of the 1988 film (developed by Pack-In-Video). John McClane fights 40 terrorists through Nakatomi Plaza while Theo cracks the vault's six locks.
entries.gameplay_notes: Clear floors of terrorists using stairs, elevators and vents opened by shooting grilles. Start with a 15-round pistol and pick up SMGs, explosives, rocket launchers and flamethrowers. Soda cans restore health. A 'foot meter' drains from running and broken glass and slows McClane when empty; med-kits refill it. Destroying the main computer buys time. Cinematics change with your actions.

difficulty.reason: Short-range shots, a timer on the vault and a foot meter that slows you down.

entries.title: Dragon Warrior

entries.title: Excitebike
entries.summary: Nintendo's 1984 side-scrolling motocross racer: qualify in the top three to reach the Excitebike championship.

entries.title: Ghosts 'n Goblins
entries.summary: NES version of Capcom's 1985 arcade platformer (converted by Micronics): the knight Sir Arthur fights through the Demon World to rescue Princess Prin-Prin from Astaroth.
entries.why_it_matters: Among the top-grossing arcade games of 1986 and a commercial success on the NES. It is often cited as one of the hardest games ever made.
entries.gameplay_notes: Two hits cost Arthur a life, sending you back to the level start or a checkpoint. Levels are timed. Some bosses can't be hurt by certain weapons. Beating Astaroth sends you through the whole game again on higher difficulty for the true ending.
